units.description: True when a character of the text starts at byte index i, for 0 <= i < len(s). Byte i starts a character when i is 0, or when byte i is not a UTF-8 continuation byte (a continuation byte is a value from 128 to 191 inclusive). Every other byte continues the character before it. Never panics for any bytes.
tests: fn cases_is_start_hexv(c: int) -> [] int { if c >= 97 { return c - 87; } return c - 48; }

fn cases_is_start_unhex[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, hex: &r [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]] { let n = len(hex) / 2; let b = box_slice(heap, n, byte_of(0)); borrow mut b as &!w in { let s = contents(w); var i = 0; while i < n { s[i] = byte_of(cases_is_start_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i])) * 16 + cases_is_start_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i + 1]))); i = i + 1; } } return b; }
pub fn test_is_start_1() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_is_start("abc", 0) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_is_start_2() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_is_start("abc", 2) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_is_start_3() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_is_start("café", 3) == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_is_start_4() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_is_start("café", 4) == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_is_start_5() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_is_start("日本語", 1) == false); return 0; }

fn cases_is_start_c6[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { let a1 = cases_is_start_unhex(heap, "a941"); var code = 1; borrow a1 as &ra1 in { if editdistance_is_start(contents(ra1), 0) == true { code = 0; } } unbox_slice(heap, a1); return code; }
pub fn test_is_start_6[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_is_start_c6(heap), 0); return 0; }

fn cases_is_start_c7[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { let a1 = cases_is_start_unhex(heap, "a941"); var code = 1; borrow a1 as &ra1 in { if editdistance_is_start(contents(ra1), 1) == true { code = 0; } } unbox_slice(heap, a1); return code; }
pub fn test_is_start_7[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_is_start_c7(heap), 0); return 0; }

units.description: The number of Unicode characters (code points) in s: the count of byte indices i, from 0 up to len(s) minus one, for which editdistance_is_start(s, i) is true. The empty text has 0. Counts characters, never bytes: "é" is 1 and "日本語" is 3. Never panics for any bytes.
tests: fn cases_chars_hexv(c: int) -> [] int { if c >= 97 { return c - 87; } return c - 48; }

fn cases_chars_unhex[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, hex: &r [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]] { let n = len(hex) / 2; let b = box_slice(heap, n, byte_of(0)); borrow mut b as &!w in { let s = contents(w); var i = 0; while i < n { s[i] = byte_of(cases_chars_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i])) * 16 + cases_chars_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i + 1]))); i = i + 1; } } return b; }
pub fn test_chars_1() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_chars("") == 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_chars_2() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_chars("abc") == 3); return 0; }
pub fn test_chars_3() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_chars("café") == 4); return 0; }
pub fn test_chars_4() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_chars("日本語") == 3); return 0; }

fn cases_chars_c5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { let a1 = cases_chars_unhex(heap, "a941"); var code = 1; borrow a1 as &ra1 in { if editdistance_chars(contents(ra1)) == 2 { code = 0; } } unbox_slice(heap, a1); return code; }
pub fn test_chars_5[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_chars_c5(heap), 0); return 0; }

units.description: Given 0 <= start < len(s) where a character starts, the byte index just past that character: the smallest j greater than start such that j equals len(s) or editdistance_is_start(s, j) is true. Its byte span is s[start..result]. Never panics for any bytes.

units.description: True exactly when x and y have the same length and the same bytes in the same order. Two empty texts are the same. Compares bytes only, never characters.
tests: pub fn test_same_1() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_same("abc", "abc") == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_2() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_same("ab", "abc") == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_3() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_same("", "") == true); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_4() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_same("", "a") == false); return 0; }
pub fn test_same_5() -> [] int { test.assert(editdistance_same("café", "cafe") == false); return 0; }

units.description: The Levenshtein distance between a and b, counted in characters: the fewest single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn a into b. Characters are the spans from editdistance_span_end; two characters are equal when editdistance_same accepts their byte spans. Let m be the number of characters of a and n of b (editdistance_chars). Use one row of n+1 ints, allocated in a region (alloc_slice with 0), and fill it by the standard single-row method: row[j] starts as j; for each character of a in order, set the diagonal value to row[0] before changing it, set row[0] to i, then for each character of b in order save the old row[j] as the next diagonal, and set row[j] to the minimum of old row[j] + 1, the new row[j-1] + 1, and the saved diagonal + cost, where cost is 0 for equal characters and 1 otherwise. The answer is row[n]. Empty text is distance 0 from the empty text and n from b. Symmetric, 0 exactly when the texts are equal. Walk characters by byte spans rather than building arrays of characters. The row lives in an arena of 64 KiB, so a text of about 8000 characters or more exhausts it and the program stops; 60 characters is far below that. Never panics for any bytes.
tests: fn cases_distance_hexv(c: int) -> [] int { if c >= 97 { return c - 87; } return c - 48; }

fn cases_distance_unhex[&h, &r](heap: &!h Heap, hex: &r [byte]) -> [heap] Box[[byte]] { let n = len(hex) / 2; let b = box_slice(heap, n, byte_of(0)); borrow mut b as &!w in { let s = contents(w); var i = 0; while i < n { s[i] = byte_of(cases_distance_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i])) * 16 + cases_distance_hexv(int_of(hex[2 * i + 1]))); i = i + 1; } } return b; }

units.description: A whole number from 0 to 100. If both texts have no characters the answer is 100. Otherwise let m be the larger of the two character counts (editdistance_chars) and d be edit_distance(a, b); the answer is (100 * (m - d)) divided by m with integer division rounding down. Always between 0 and 100. Never panics for any bytes.

pub fn test_similarity_2() -> [] int { test.assert(similarity_pct("", "") == 100); return 0; }

units.description: The candidate, as the same text reference that was passed in, with the smallest edit_distance to query. Walk candidates in order from index 0, keeping the best candidate and its distance; replace the best only when a candidate's distance is strictly smaller, so the first of several ties wins. Return Some(best) when there is at least one candidate, and None for an empty list. Read the vec with the std.vec operations and import std.vec and std.option as needed. Never panics for any text.
tests: fn cases_closest_same[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn cases_closest_some[&t1, &v2, &e2, &w](a1: &t1 [byte], a2: &v2 vec.Vec[&e2 [byte]], want: &w [byte]) -> [] int { match closest(a1, a2) { option.Option::Some(v) => { if cases_closest_same(v, want) { return 0; } return 1; } option.Option::None => { return 2; } } }
fn cases_closest_none[&t1, &v2, &e2](a1: &t1 [byte], a2: &v2 vec.Vec[&e2 [byte]]) -> [] int { match closest(a1, a2) { option.Option::Some(_) => { return 2; } option.Option::None => { return 0; } } }

fn cases_closest_c1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var a2 = vec.empty(heap, 3, ""); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "abd"); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "abe"); var code = 1; borrow a2 as &ra2 in { code = cases_closest_some("abc", ra2, "abd"); } vec.drop(heap, a2); return code; }
pub fn test_closest_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_closest_c1(heap), 0); return 0; }

fn cases_closest_c2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var a2 = vec.empty(heap, 5, ""); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "sitting"); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "mitten"); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "bitten"); a2 = vec.push(heap, a2, "kitchen"); var code = 1; borrow a2 as &ra2 in { code = cases_closest_some("kitten", ra2, "mitten"); } vec.drop(heap, a2); return code; }
pub fn test_closest_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_closest_c2(heap), 0); return 0; }
fn cases_closest_c3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { var a2 = vec.empty(heap, 1, ""); var code = 1; borrow a2 as &ra2 in { code = cases_closest_none("x", ra2); } vec.drop(heap, a2); return code; }
pub fn test_closest_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(cases_closest_c3(heap), 0); return 0; }
